experiment.title: Northstar × Utopia · scale (large)
experiment.status_note: Scale arm done. Graph-only reader: curated facts + OWM procedure + request record → 13/15, 15/15 once the agreement term is curated. All-tools reader with the same OWM inputs: 15/15 on the curated and the uncurated graph, including a leak-free control. Curation is only needed for graph-only consumers.

findings.title: Facts + procedure + request record: 13 of 15 at scale
findings.body: On the curated scale graph, the blind graph-only reader with the OWM procedure and the CRM request record matches the answer key on S01, S02, S04 and S05 in 3 of 3 runs, and on S03 in 1 of 3 (15 of 15 at small scale). Both misses answer REQUEST_EVIDENCE instead of REVIEW_REQUIRED: the graph's "Master Supply Agreement" is a name with no facts at scale, so the procedure's ask-for-the-document rule fires. Every miss declines to approve; none is an unsafe decision.

findings.title: Without facts, the procedure makes the reader ask instead of guess
findings.body: On the uncurated scale graph, the same reader with the procedure answers REQUEST_EVIDENCE on all five decisions, listing the exception maximum, validity dates and approval bands as missing. By the fixed rule that is 0 pass, 1 partial and 4 fail, but no decision approves or rejects on a guess. Curation is what turns these into correct decisions.

findings.title: Text retrieval is unaffected by 10× noise
findings.body: B1 (all tools, uncurated) grades 9 pass and 1 partial, identical to the small run down to the same S03 framing ("needs VP sign-off" rather than commercial review).

findings.title: The 15% and the agreement's terms never reached the graph
findings.body: At small scale one fact carried the agreement's sentence "eligible for discounts of up to 15% on the NS-500" as its quote, and graph-only readers found it by digging `changes`. At scale no fact from the agreement or the 2025 exception carries 15%. The exception came out as structure only, and the agreement entity has no facts (1 at small scale). B2 therefore never finds 15%, and it gives the old exception's dates to the new one: 2 pass, 7 partial and 1 fail, against 6 pass and 4 partial at small scale.

findings.title: A bare "Acme" attached to the wrong customer
findings.body: In both scale KBs the email's bare "Acme" became a name of Acme Industrial Supply Co. In missing-contract, "asking for 15% off list" was attached there too. A graph-only reader reported it on S05. The small-run KBs don't have this attachment.

findings.title: Most of the review queue was governance stalled by the spend limit
findings.body: The 2,763 and 3,828 pending duplicate pairs at settle were mostly pairs the governance agent never reached: every hourly run failed on the OpenAI spend limit from 01:08. Once the limit was raised, governance cleared the backlog in 23 minutes, and 232 and 203 pairs are left for a human (about 40–46× the small run's 5).

findings.title: Curation pushes resolved without a human
findings.body: The Statements push minted duplicate Sarah Chen and David Morgan entities in base. Utopia's adjudicator merged both into the existing people at 0.90 within 22 seconds, and no review was queued. At small scale the same kind of duplicates waited for a human at 0.52–0.54.

findings.title: The org chart produced no reporting lines at scale
findings.body: The org chart's 3 chunks yielded titles, name facts and em-dash phrases, but no `reports to`. At small scale the lines came out inverted; at scale they are missing. Same document, different failure. Curation pushed all 43 lines from the chart.

findings.title: The RDF export is refused at scale
findings.body: Base export: 422 unexported_target, fact.object(merged): 152 rows, before and after settling. The declared machine-readable read contract (ADR 0020) is unavailable exactly when a KB is big enough to need it. The missing-contract export works (11.7 MB). Upstream issue 6.

findings.title: No CSV truncation at scale
findings.body: Every small-run CSV had a truncated_reply drop; at scale none do, with tables chunked about 3 rows per chunk. DR-9001 keeps its justification in base. In missing-contract it lost the justification anyway (5 fields).

findings.title: One curated fact closes the S03 split
findings.body: Adding the single agreement fact the small graph had ("Master Supply Agreement is effective", 2025-04-01..2028-03-31, from §1 of the agreement) to the curated scale graph turns S03 from 1 of 3 to 3 of 3. Every run now establishes the agreement as active, finds no NS-Cloud term, and answers REVIEW_REQUIRED with the right approver. The scale miss was the foundation dropping one fact, not reader noise. With it, the decision scenarios are 15 of 15 on the curated scale graph (S01, S02, S04 and S05 from the B2kPR runs; S03 from this check).

findings.title: With text retrieval, the OWM layer needs no curation: 15/15 uncurated
findings.body: The all-tools reader with the OWM procedure and the request record decides S01–S05 correctly on every scored field in 3 of 3 runs, on the curated graph (B1kPR), with curation withdrawn (B1PR), and in the control with `changes` hidden so no withdrawn value can leak (B1nPR): 45 of 45. It reads the facts from the source documents (96 search_chunks and 33 get_document calls in the control), in 9–25 turns against 21–43 for graph-only. Curation is only needed when the reader is restricted to the graph. For these decisions the foundation's job is evidence retrieval and identity; the OWM supplies the procedure, the request record and the decision record.

findings.title: Withdrawn statements stay readable in `changes`
findings.body: Withdrawing a Statements push (tombstone + missing-cleanup) retracts its facts and restores the live counts exactly, but the record-time audit feed keeps each retraction as a `rejected` event with the fact's value. 11 of 15 uncurated B1 answers saw withdrawn curation values that way. It's correct audit behaviour, but an experiment that withdraws facts must hide `changes` (the B1n variant) or treat the arm as contaminated.
